items.description:
The event aimed to leverage Roche’s Oncology outcomes, engage stakeholders, and stimulate networking.
Commercialisation Excellence (MTO: 4): The goal was to deliver differentiated, personalized, and patient-focused solutions to solidify Roche as a preferred partner.
Shifting Congress Management (STO): The focus was on moving towards an outcome-focused approach, enabling Healthcare Professionals (HCPs) to experience elevated, collaborative engagements that build trust and loyalty.
items.learnings:
Power of the Network: The team reinforced the idea that "when we come together great things happen," successfully creating a template for "above country collaboration".
Planning Horizon: A critical takeaway was the necessity of a 6-month lead time. Earlier planning would have significantly benefited the omnichannel strategy and logistics.
Regional Insights: The team observed similar healthcare system challenges across Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) and identified continued opportunities to make an impact with the HER2 franchise.
Strategic Alignment:  Difference in country priority products -SA  focus on Phesgo & Tecentriq -Lung, resulted in lack of collateral for Perjeta, Herceptin & Tecentriq HCC at the booth.
Earlier Action: Planning must start early to avoid the "last minute rush" regarding speaker identification, contracting, and accommodation bookings.
Achieve Logistical Autonomy: Reduce dependency on hosting country teams for administrative support by engaging specialized event-planning partners and leveraging above-country expertise.
Better Data & Feedback: There is a strong desire for improved data on booth attendance and "Voice of Customer" (VoC) feedback to aid follow-up conversations. This includes collaborating with global VoC experts for better survey design.
Shared Workload: To reduce dependency on the host country, the team intends to leverage expertise in other affiliates to distribute tasks more effectively.
Optimize Engagement Modalities: Actively leverage high-touch opportunities such as roundtables and HCP interviews to maximize the opportunity for deep scientific exchange
Technical Accountability: Require an earlier brief to the LAB team to ensure all assets are interfaced into epicX and that attendance data flows directly into OCE for personalized engagement
Enhanced Affiliate Alignment: Mandate regular alignment meetings between affiliates regarding delegate lists and local content needs, fostering a culture where challenges are shared proactively

subitems: EMSO BC Congress HCPs sponsorships, speaker contracting and Case Study Clinics  preparation and execution
items.description:
Meet the Expert Case Rotations replace traditional lectures with a high-energy "speed dating" approach to clinical education. In a series of timed roundtable rotations, HCPs collaborate with Global  TAEs to dissect the most complex early Breast Cancer (eBC) cases. This dynamic setup fosters a rigorous academic exchange, allowing participants to address real-world challenges directly and translate expert insights into immediate, practical clinical solutions.
This WP is designed to align our congress plans with the broader Africa network approach, maximizing HCP engagements to deliver on relevant MTOs.
The core purpose is to enhance Roche's position as a unified, innovative healthcare solutions provider in Africa. We achieve this by enabling HCPs to experience elevated, collaborative congress engagements, which are intended to drive long-term value,  build trust, loyalty, and stronger partnerships.
items.learnings:
Varied Regional Challenges: Africa shares highly similar healthcare system challenges regarding breast cancer management. Addressing these collectively under a unified banner ("Putting Her First") yields far greater stakeholder impact than working in silos.
The 6-Month Horizon Rule: To effectively coordinate international speakers, execute contracts, and secure smooth delegate management, a hard 6-month lead time must be institutionalized.
Event Strategy: The meeting validated the interactive table-based format as highly successful. Future side events will prioritize scheduling one day prior to the congress to reduce attendee fatigue and maximize engagement, ensuring a balanced approach to regional vs. international content.
Speaker & Moderator Strategy: A balanced speaker composition strategy will be adopted, blending international experts with regional voices. Local moderators are identified as critical for effective, culturally relevant communication.
Post-Event Communication: A bifurcated communication strategy will be implemented: one track for participants thanking them and gathering feedback via a concise, single-question survey, and a second track for general distribution of highlights and presentation materials via newsletters.
Internal Communication: Future alignment will be maintained through consistent internal updates, with identified POCs established to streamline the dissemination of event summaries via RocheNet.

The Power of Pan-African Collaboration : Pan-African expert collaboration establishes a vital, standardized clinical baseline tailored to regional realities
Realistic Guidelines: Consensus statements must prioritize achievable clinical minimums for resource-constrained settings over unattainable global ideals.

Technical Preparation: Digital polling mechanics and unambiguous voting statements must be finalized and tested well before the live session.
Session Limits: Interactive virtual events must be kept well under 3 hours to prevent participant fatigue and to sustain energy.

items.itemName: C2 STO 1 TW- SK Surgeons ABM
items.description:
In Taiwan and South Korea, surgeons are pivotal decision-makers in the treatment of breast cancer. The evolving HER2-positive landscape, with the introduction of new agents alongside PHESGO, has created a more complex treatment paradigm.
To maintain PH's leadership in early breast cancer (eBC), we must clearly define its value in the neoadjuvant setting and refine the post-surgical strategy for patients with either a pathological complete response (pCR) or residual disease (RD).
In metastatic breast cancer (mBC), while the PH-based regimen is the established first-line standard of care, the upcoming DESTINY-Breast09 data requires us to proactively frame the efficacy-versus-toxicity trade-off to ensure optimal treatment sequencing and long-term survival.
This advisory board is crucial for gathering expert insights to reinforce the comprehensive value of PH—its proven efficacy, manageable safety, and the convenience of its subcutaneous formulation—as a cornerstone of care in both eBC and mBC.

To motivate HCPs more, we should bridge the gap between clinical efficacy and the experience of living with cancer. The core input for this initiative will be a collection of powerful, authentic patient and caregiver stories. Our success is interdependent on our ability to not only gather these narratives and make videos of patient story and HCP testimonial but also to equip teams with the emotional storytelling skills needed to convey the profound impact that a treatment choice like PHESGO can have on a patient's quality of life, not just their clinical outcome.

The emphasis is on external activities that accelerate clinical adoption and stakeholder confidence by leveraging the credibility of experienced experts and markets.

Through expert roundtables, and real-world experience sharing sessions, early adopters will showcase how they achieved successful guideline integration, and clinical uptake. items.itemName: Hemlibra_C2 C3 2025_Building a voice of Haemophilia
subitems: Methodology and execution of focus group and in depth interviews
items.description:
Despite compelling individual stories, there's a critical lack of consolidated data on the comprehensive challenges faced by Singaporean haemophilia patients and caregivers, encompassing physical, quality of life, productivity, and economic burdens. This data gap impedes effective advocacy and support. 
The focus group and survey aims to systematically collect vital qualitative and quantitative insights, which will then guide HSS in developing more effective support programs and inform our efforts to develop advocates for Hemlibra within HSS.

To build a Treatment Impact Model (TIM) to quantify the number of events (bleeds, hospitalisation days, etc.) averted and downstream costs saved with Hemlibra available, using several uptake scenarios.

- Drive critical benchmarking of Singapore’s hemophilia care practices against leading-edge models (e.g., Australia, New Zealand), prompting the identification and adoption of actionable improvements in local clinical practice.
- Local hematologists and emerging physicians integrate global best practices and regional innovations into their clinical routines, resulting in more informed and effective patient management strategies.
Empower emerging local physicians (P3) to develop broader perspectives and build confidence by engaging with a diverse panel of international and regional experts, accelerating their professional growth into future leaders in hemophilia care.
- Foster sustained relationships between Singapore-based clinicians and international hematology leaders, leading to  future partnerships, joint initiatives, and knowledge exchange.

items.description:
Retina ExchANGe Webinars: The C.O.R.E (Comprehensive Ophthalmic Retina Education) Academy
This strategic workpackage launches a 2-season educational program designed to empower general ophthalmologists/new retina specialist (P1-P2-P3-P4)  across Vietnam. It addresses the core challenges preventing widespread treatment of retinal disease (nAMD, DME, RVO, PCV): diagnostic (OCT) uncertainty, procedural fears, and the immense "treatment burden" of frequent-injection protocols.
The C.O.R.E curriculum progresses from foundational injection skills to advanced patient management. It strategically integrates Faricimab (Vabysmo), showcasing its unique dual Ang-2/VEGF mechanism as the scientific solution to treatment burden and refractory cases.
The objective is to build universal physician confidence, solve systemic practice challenges via Faricimab's Q16W durability, and establish it as the new, definitive standard of care for retinal diseases in all Eye hospitals and general hospitals.

items.itemName: Round Table ,,Sharing 1 year experience with Hemlibra''
items.description: Conduct a roundtable discussion, "Sharing 1-Year Experience with Hemlibra," to bring HCPs together to exchange insights on treatment outcomes. The session will also showcase data on 8 newly added patients (4 adults and 4 pediatric) after 34 weeks of the loading dose, emphasizing clinical impact and driving further adoption of Hemlibra in eligible patient populations.
items.realizedHWWK:
The activity, centered around the "Sharing 1-Year Experience with Hemlibra" roundtable, successfully achieved two primary outcomes while clearly identifying two critical adoption barriers.

1.  Positive Clinical and Adoption Outcomes
Increased HCP Confidence and Engagement: The roundtable format was effective in showcasing the drug's real-world value by sharing the positive treatment journey of existing patients.

Demonstration of Efficacy: The activity successfully presented data on 8 newly added patients (4 adults and 4 pediatric), proving Hemlibra's utility across diverse demographics and reinforcing positive treatment outcomes after one year.

Identification of New Candidates: The discussion went beyond existing patients, successfully identifying and presenting new cases that could immediately benefit from Hemlibra therapy.

2. Critical Barriers to Be Addressed
The direct feedback from the HCPs at the roundtable highlighted the main hurdles for further widespread adoption:

Budget Allocation: The primary financial barrier is the difficulty in securing adequate budget allocation or funding for Hemlibra within current institutional frameworks.

Diagnostic Tools: A key logistical/clinical challenge is the lack of readily available diagnostic tools, specifically for the accurate measurement of inhibitor levels in hemophilia patients.

items.description: Spinal Muscular Atrophy (SMA) is no longer viewed through a singular lens; it is a rare, multisystemic pathology that requires personalized approach. Central to modern management is the critical window of opportunity for early therapeutic intervention, as timely treatment is paramount to halting irreversible neuronal loss. Our mission is to empower healthcare professionals with the knowledge to navigate this evolving landscape—from rapid clinical recognition and genetic insights to comprehensive, long-term systemic management.  The landscape of Spinal Muscular Atrophy (SMA) has transitioned from a period of limited options to an era of rapid therapeutic innovation, yet significant gaps remain in early diagnosis and holistic, long-term management. To strengthen our position, as the preferred partner in this space, we must move beyond being a service provider to becoming a central pillar of the ecosystem. Through collaborative projects and targeted digital campaigns towards identified audience, we intend to position Roche as the preferred partner of the SMA community.

items.itemName: Expanding Access to Innovation in Punjab
subitems: KOL Advocacy & Support Mobilization in Policy Shaping
Strengthen Roche’s Position as a Trusted Partner
items.description:
Through a public–private partnership with the Government of Punjab, Roche aims to make its innovative therapies accessible to non-affording patients in all Public hospitals. This initiative will enable patients to benefit from lifesaving and disease-modifying treatment , reduce financial hardship for families and contribute to improved survival and quality of life outcomes. 
For Roche, the collaboration reinforces our role as a trusted healthcare partner, strengthens our leadership in priority therapeutic areas, and creates a scalable model for patient access that can be replicated across other provinces. Importantly, the initiative is fully aligned with our Therapeutic Area (TA) outcomes, supporting the mission to ensure equitable and timely access to breakthrough innovations where the unmet medical need is greatest.
Key Deliverables:
Leverage Real-World Evidence (RWE): Utilize available RWE in Oncology, Multiple Sclerosis, and Ophthalmology to demonstrate the clinical and societal value of Roche’s innovative therapies.
Engage Key Opinion Leaders (KOLs): Collaborate with identified  KOLs and technical experts who are prepared to advocate for the positive impact of Roche’s medicines, reinforcing credibility if consulted by the Government.
Strengthen Roche’s Position as a Trusted Partner: Build on Roche’s established reputation to engage the Government of Punjab in meaningful dialogue on the value of innovation and sustainable healthcare solutions.
Promote Long-Term Societal Impact: Highlight how access to innovative medicines can improve patient outcomes, reduce healthcare burden, and deliver measurable benefits to society over time.

To secure a favorable EDL recommendation by mobilizing a unified front of clinical experts and Patient Advocacy Groups (PAGs) to demonstrate the therapeutic value of Lunsumio.

Core Activities
Expert Mobilization: Briefing key opinion leaders (KOLs) to provide clinical testimony on the benefits of "off-the-shelf" bispecific therapy.
PAG Advocacy: Partnering with patient groups to highlight the unmet need and quality-of-life improvements in follicular lymphoma.
Evidence Synthesis: Developing concise briefing materials and FAQ sets to address potential Commission concerns regarding safety (CRS) and infrastructure.
Strategic Alignment: Facilitating consensus meetings to ensure a consistent message across all stakeholders during the hearing.

Objective
To compile and submit the formal regulatory and economic dossier required to secure an OMItariff for Polivy ensuring its reimbursement for eligible lymphoma patients.
Dossier Compilation: Preparing the technical submission, including clinical efficacy summaries from pivotal trials (e.g., POLARIX) and safety data.
Tariff Calculation: Determining the proposed reimbursement rate based on dosing schedules, hospital administration costs, and regional pricing benchmarks.
Regulatory Liaison: Managing the submission timeline and responding to technical clarifications or "Requests for Information" from the OMI Commission.

items.description:
We have identified a critical need for advanced clinical education among hematologists regarding the rapidly evolving treatment landscape of DLBCL. By attending this preceptorship, participant will gain comprehensive insights into: precision diagnostics of DLBCL, use of Bispecific vs. Cell therapy and about management of complex cases.
This deeper knowledge empowers HCPs to adopt bispecific treatments with confidence. This directly correlates with our STO by positioning Columvi as the preferred therapy in 2L DLBCL. By equipping clinicians to navigate these innovations, we facilitate broader access via Article 22, ensuring that patients with high unmet needs receive timely and appropriate treatment.

This work package facilitates a high-level regional meeting for experts from Serbia, Montenegro, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and North Macedonia, designed to harmonize Hemophilia A management through collaborative scientific exchange. The primary outcome is to establish a unified regional approach to therapeutic paradigms and clinical monitoring, driven by the active participation of local experts in program preparation and regional panels. Success will be validated by the presence of the most relevant regional stakeholders and the delivery of a comprehensive meeting report mapping the clinical journey, treatment availability, and future directions for hemophilia care across the participating countries.

This work package provides educational support for multidisciplinary healthcare professionals to attend the 63rd Oncology Congress in Belgrade. The primary objective is to advance clinical expertise in novel breast cancer treatment strategies among physicians while empowering nursing staff with updated knowledge on patient care management. By facilitating participation in key scientific sessions, this initiative aims to strengthen cross-functional collaboration and optimize the overall patient journey in routine clinical practice.

items.itemName: HR+ and HER2+ mBC landscape Advisory Board: where we are today and where we are heading tomorrow?
items.description: This Advisory Board will gather expert clinical insights on the current patient pathway -encompassing diagnosis, testing protocols, and therapeutic management - for HR+/HER2- breast cancer in Montenegro, with a primary focus on metastatic disease (mBC). The discussions will aim to quantify the eligible patient population for the inavolisib (INAVO) regimen and assess its clinical utility in managing endocrine-resistant HR+/HER2- mBC. Furthermore, the board will evaluate the feasibility, integration, and clinical impact of implementing routine PIK3CA mutation reflex testing into local diagnostic practice.

items.description: Establish Vabysmo as the first-line /first choice

Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is one of the leading causes of cancer-related mortality globally, with a significant proportion of patients diagnosed at the intermediate stage (BCLC-B). Traditionally, intermediate HCC has been managed with locoregional therapies (LRT), primarily Transarterial Chemoembolization (TACE), based on historical standards of care.
The treatment landscape in advanced/unresectable HCC (uHCC) has evolved significantly with the advent of immunotherapy-based combinations such as atezolizumab plus bevacizumab and other IO-based regimens, demonstrating meaningful survival benefit and durable responses.
Recently, emerging evidence is beginning to challenge the conventional paradigm in intermediate HCC:
The TALENTACE study explored the integration of systemic immunotherapy-based combinations with TACE in intermediate-stage disease, suggesting improved response rates and potential survival benefit.


The ABC-HCC trial evaluated upfront systemic therapy in intermediate HCC compared to conventional TACE, raising important questions about optimal sequencing and patient selection.


These data signal a potential paradigm shift — from TACE alone toward:
Combination strategies (Systemic therapy + TACE)


Upfront systemic therapy in selected intermediate HCC patients


Given the heterogeneity within BCLC-B disease and the evolving evidence base, there is a critical need to understand the clinical practice impact that this emerging evidence could have on the optimized treatment algorithm.

items.itemName: Project RAPID - Real-Time Analysis and Prediction for Informed Decisions
items.description: For Finance, Business Excellence, and Commercial functions who struggle with complex, manual data compilation that creates a 'Real-Time Visibility Gap,' the Project RAPID solution is an Agentic AI "Super-radar" that automatically synthesizes internal and external (both unstructured and structured) data 24/7 to reduce administrative time by ~80% and enables proactive, predictive forecasting. Unlike our current manual, reactive scanning processes, our solution leverages autonomous AI on the enterprise-validated Dataiku platform to continuously monitor, analyze, and trigger strategic alerts, allowing teams to shift their focus from data gathering to high-impact decision-making.
items.realizedHWWK:
- Functional Completion: The specific automated data pipeline or AI agent component has been built and successfully executes without errors.
- Data Integration Verified: The component successfully ingests and synthesizes the intended internal and/or external data sources (structured and unstructured) as defined in the technical requirements.
- Performance Criteria Met: The solution demonstrates the expected reduction in manual processing or achieves the targeted "Super-radar" monitoring capability as planned.
- Quality Assurance: The output (e.g., alerts, forecasts, synthesized data sets) has been validated for accuracy and relevance against the manual "current state" process to ensure the AI's "predictive advantage" is reliable.
- Documentation: Technical documentation and user workflows for the new component are updated, ensuring that the team understands how to use the automated insights for decision-making.
- Stakeholder Acceptance: The specific output or feature has been reviewed and accepted by the project leads and other stakeholders (e.g. Finance Reshape Team, Sponsor)
- Scalability Proof: The PoC/PoV successfully demonstrates that the solution architecture and data models are replicable across different market environments, confirming its readiness and ability to scale effectively to multiple affiliates.

This gig advances Roche’s global Ophthalmology vision of preventing vision loss and restoring vision where disease prevention is too late by strengthening the policy environment for eye health innovation across Central and Eastern Europe (CEE).

Building on Roche’s Ophthalmology strategy to maximize current retinal leadership, expand beyond VEGF, and pioneer transformative innovation in glaucoma and dry eye disease, this initiative focuses on translating scientific progress into sustainable policy action.

The gig supports Roche’s pillars of:
Patient impact & access – elevating unmet needs in retinal, glaucoma, and diabetic eye disease
Innovation leadership – enabling adoption of next-generation therapies and diagnostics
Health system strengthening – improving early detection, referral pathways, and integrated care
Partnership & trust – mobilising multi-stakeholder coalitions across CEE
Our vision: CEE people with /or at a risk of visual impairment due to nAMD / DME / RVO have timely access to diagnosis and innovative treatment thanks to the increased eye health priority and Governments’ readiness to fund policies aimed at tackling the personal, social, and economic burden of vision loss.

The work builds directly on the 2025 WP “Increasing Vision Health Priority & Awareness in the CEE region”:

The findings of the IQVIA CEE Ecosystem study
The first meeting of the CEE Retina PAGs in Budapest
The multistakeholder policy meeting in Rome
The CEE Retina PAGs White Paper
Ongoing engagement with patient organizations, policymakers, clinicians, and payers
Wealth of data on cost to society and societal value of innovation

The focus now shifts from strategy to tactical implementation, using targeted regional and national national platforms to embed innovation in eye health into policy agendas.

items.learnings:
Reflecting on our Traditional SMA Community Workshop: Building a Partnership Rooted in Trust
This year’s edition of our traditional workshop for patients with spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) and their caregivers once again proved how vital the voice of the community truly is. When organizing this event, we always build directly upon the real needs expressed by the patients themselves.
Key Takeaways from This Year's Event:
•	Organizing with them, not just for them: Involving patients from the very initial planning stages is the best way to ensure high attendance and active engagement.
•	Building trust: This approach is absolutely essential for strengthening mutual trust and positioning Roche as a visible, reliable partner for the SMA community.
Practical Tips for Future Logistics:
•	Accessibility first: It is crucial to select venues with extreme care to guarantee 100% barrier-free access.
•	An individualized approach: Every SMA patient and their caregiver have highly specific, individual needs that we must anticipate and accommodate in advance.
•	Continuity through feedback: Sending out a post-event feedback questionnaire is a must. The insights gathered serve as a valuable source of inspiration and topics for our next gatherings.

items.itemName: MR | OCREVUS U&A Study 2026 aCD20 doferenciace
items.description: OCREVUS U&A Study 2026 aCD20 doferenciace; RS centra

This Work Package establishes a flexible, evolving medical strategy targeting high-potential, independent prescribers identified as low-to-mid adopters of Vabysmo (faricimab). Covering a broad retinal scope - initially prioritized for neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD) and diabetic macular edema (DME), with adaptability for retinal vein occlusion (RVO) - this strategy addresses core clinical barriers through a hybrid engagement model. By deploying 1:1 dialogues, regional advisory touchpoints, and medical education, the initiative delivers rigorous scientific data on dual Ang-2/VEGF-A pathway inhibition, rapid fluid drying, and treat-and-extend (T&E) durability to build clinician confidence and support optimal patient selection. HCP targeting will undergo major updates based on 120D Squad Meeting outcomes and will also be updated on a continuous basis.

This WP establishes a pre-launch medical strategy and Pre-Approval Access Program (PAAP, SLP) framework for vamikibart (Ivamky), an investigational intravitreal anti-IL-6 monoclonal antibody. Focused on uveitic macular edema (UME) secondary to non-infectious uveitis (NIU), this strategy addresses critical unmet clinical needs in patients who are steroid-refractory, steroid-intolerant, at high risk for corticosteroid-induced complications (such as intraocular pressure spikes or cataracts) or where corticosteroid treatment is not necessary. By driving non-promotional scientific exchange on IL-6 pathway inhibition, establishing compliant processes to manage unsolicited early-access requests, and mapping clinical management gaps, this initiative prepares the expert community for targeted non-steroid intravitreal therapy while enabling urgent patient access prior to commercial authorization.

items.description:
The Challenge: Currently, innovative care is often hindered by dosage form determinants, which act as gatekeepers to access: the administration format (IV vs. SC) dictates the funding channel—locking treatments into either strained local HVA budgets or the national reimbursement system. This 'funding lottery' based on the dosage form—rather than clinical need—determines whether an innovative medicine is actually available to the patient.

Roche Finland is applying reimbursement for four hospital medicines: PHESGO SC, Tecentriq SC, Ocrevus SC and Vabysmo. 

Our Vision:
National Equity: Innovative treatments must be available equally across Finland. By securing national reimbursement through the "Access Hack," we remove local financial barriers and ensure that geography no longer defines the quality of care.

Physician Empowerment: We ensure doctors have a full range of options. Medical appropriateness—not the constraints of a specific budgets —must be the sole driver of the treatment decision.

Clinical Freedom: Transitioning to the national budget allows physicians to choose the most effective setting for care (e.g., decentralized units) without burdening the hospital's operational resources.

items.itemName: Shared Decision Making in MS - Collaboration with MS Ireland
items.description:
Insights from our IQVIA market research show that just over half of patients prescribed a DMT are presented with full optionality at the point of decision-making. In 36% of instances where Mavenclad is prescribed, the patient made the final treatment selection. This suggests that when patients are left to make decisions themselves, they place high importance on convenience.

Insights from the Global Patient Partnership team and patient communities indicate a need for a consistent, systematic approach to support patients with decision-making and treatment selection. Shared decision-making (SDM) is a form of patient-centered communication that is gaining traction, given the evidence of its importance for individualising treatment, improving adherence, and more.

RPIL plans to explore a collaborative agreement with MS Ireland to co-develop an SDM framework to support MS treatment decisions, leveraging MS Ireland’s consultative fora. RPIL will contribute insights from the clinical community to the framework and identify clinical champions to socialise the framework and ensure its adoption among clinicians.

Collaborate with MS Ireland to update the MS Ireland MS Explained booklet to include a new segment on Shared Decision Making in MS. To this end, and through this material, we aim to ensure patients are fully empowered to ask questions relevant to their MS care and specifically treatment selection, thereby encouraging patients to consider full treatment optionality.

The booklet will be launched at the MS Ireland 2026 conference in October (Friday October 16th / Saturday October 17th).  As part of this launch a comprehensive communications plan is being co-created with MS Ireland to drive awareness of this new segment within the booklet and of the importance of shared decision making and patient empowerment when it comes to the selection of the most suitable treatment for each individual patient.

items.itemName: Neuro Long Term Patient Engagement Strategy
items.description:
Building on the success of the #MyNeurologyNurseAndMe campaign with the NAI we aim to drive investment in MS specialist nurses over the long term. This is to ensure sustainable access for patients to these critical supports across the end-to-end patient journey, and that the MS specialist nursing community is equipped to fully support patients with treatment-related decisions relevant to Roche.

To this end, we aim to establish an MS specialist nursing forum which, with our support, would lead on:
1)	Advocating and lobbying for increased investment in neurology services, specifically additional posts for ANPs in neurology units across the country
2)	Driving the development of resources including a comprehensive decision-support tool to ensure patients are fully informed of the full high-efficacy therapeutic optionality for MS, and that a shared-decision making process is employed at the point of treatment selection to ensure patient preferences are fully incorporated in decisions. 

It is our aim to drive the initial establishment of the group, which would then operate independently with our ad-hoc support, such as hosting meetings and helping them to develop business cases. 

From a national policy perspective, we will continue working with the NAI and MS Ireland to drive further awareness of the importance of investing in MS specialist nurses and additional posts, as well as visibility for the newly established MS specialist nursing community.

Insights from market research show that just over half of patients prescribed a DMT are presented with full optionality at the point of decision-making. In 36% of instances where Mavenclad is prescribed, the patient made the final treatment selection. This suggests that when patients are left to make decisions themselves, they place high importance on convenience. Additionally, insights from the field indicate a lack of awareness about Ocrevus and gaps in patient education about treatment optionality.

To address these gaps,  RPIL plans to collaborate with MS Ireland to update the MS Ireland MS Explained booklet to include a new segment on Shared Decision Making in MS. To this end, and through this material, we aim to ensure patients are fully empowered to ask questions relevant to their MS care and specifically treatment selection, thereby encouraging patients to consider full treatment optionality.

The booklet will be launched at the MS Ireland 2026 conference in October (Friday October 16th / Saturday October 17th).  As part of this launch a comprehensive communications plan is being co-created with MS Ireland to drive awareness of this new segment within the booklet and of the importance of shared decision making and patient empowerment when it comes to the selection of the most suitable treatment for each individual patient.

MS Explained is a comprehensive manual provided to all new MS patients at the point of diagnosis.

Working in conjunction with Dr Kilmartin, we propose to run a national meeting with invited international speakers on the topic of fast switch and suboptimal response to anti VEGF. This meeting will take place in REEV on 5th Nov. Our goal is to maximise the event and create as many assets as possible from it.

items.itemName: DELETE - P&R System - End to End Review
items.description:
The upcoming End-to-End Review of the pricing and reimbursement process represents a critical juncture for the Irish healthcare system. Following the MAAF Subgroup Workshop on 29 July 2026, the Irish Pharmaceutical Healthcare Association (IPHA) has synthesised a comprehensive strategic position to guide our engagement with the State and the appointed consultancy.
Ireland must match the ambition of its international peers. For example, the UK’s NICE established a robust 5-year strategy in 2020, centred on rapid access to the most innovative treatments. Ireland’s stakeholders must demonstrate a similar level of published, strategic ambition. To achieve this, the reimbursement process requires profound structural reform, enhanced transparency, and rigorous statutory accountability.

This workpackage outlines the strategic execution framework for Roche’s partnership with the All-Island Cancer Research Institute (AICRI) for the National Cancer Mission Hub Launch Symposium & ECHOS Summit (3–4 December 2026).

By securing a tailored strategic partnership in place of a standard Gold Sponsorship, Roche positions itself as a chosen thought partner in shaping the national cancer policy agenda. The core objective is to direct the summit's policy dialogue toward Roche’s system-shaping priorities—specifically advocating for the establishment of an Irish Early Access Programme (EAP) in oncology and demonstrating the broader societal value of early innovation access.

Strategic Partnership Execution: Establish Roche as a premier partner for AICRI’s EU Presidency Associated Event, securing high-impact agenda placement.

Agenda & Policy Shaping: Align the Slot 2 (Cancer Inequalities) agenda to focus explicitly on early access mechanisms and societal value.

Leverage the Dutch Europe's Choice Campaign to change the societal and policy narrative from a deeply ingrained belief that innovative medicines are a cost drive, to a belief that innovative medicines and healthcare is a strategic sector and asset for the Netherlands, therefore investment in healthcare, innovative medicines, and health technology not only improves outcomes for patients but also strengthens innovation, productivity, and long-term economic resilience. Positioning the campaign diplomatically to fundamentally change the relationship between the government and the sector from one of mistrust to structured cooperation, we aim to build a future-proof, accessible, and innovation-friendly pharmaceutical ecosystem in the Netherlands that drastically reduces patient access wait times, while increasing value recognition of innovative medicines.

National Economic Footprint: Research shows that clinical trials alone deliver over €1.2 billion a year in the Netherlands, underscoring pharmaceuticals as a crucial engine for economic growth and innovation resilience.

items.description:
This Work Package focuses on fundamental behavioral change within the Dutch neurology community: shifting from an "escalation" mindset to the immediate initiation of High-Efficacy Treatment (HET) at diagnosis. Currently, many Dutch neurologists wait for breakthrough disease activity before prescribing intensive therapy. Our goal is to establish "Treat Early" as the clinical default to prevent irreversible disability. Background and purpose
Shift the Dutch MS treatment paradigm from "step-care escalation" to "Early HET" (Flipping the Pyramid), to improve long term outcomes. This addresses the ~33% untreated pwMS and ~70% of treated pwMS still receiving low-efficacy therapy.

This involves aligning medical protocols with the "MS as one progressive disease" concept, ensuring that the window of opportunity for the patient is not lost

items.description:
At Roche, we believe that advanced scientific insights should not remain strictly within the medical community, but should actively serve patients to improve their quality of life. Our purpose is to empower MS patients to truly lead Shared Decision-Making (SDM) and confidently exercise their right to informed freedom of choice throughout their care path.

By leveraging Roche’s scientific expertise, we aim to demystify complex medical paradigms—enabling patients to fundamentally understand their treatment options. This includes critical concepts such as HET vs. LET, different routes of administration, on-label vs. off-label usage, and the clinical value of monitoring biomarkers like Neurofilament Light (NfL). Roche positions itself as a trusted partner that bridges the gap between high-science and patient autonomy.

items.itemName: PT_ HEMO - S3.26 - XIV Congresso da APIH
items.description:
O Congresso da APIH reúne os imunohemoterapeutas do país. Embora historicamente este evento não abordasse coagulopatias congénitas, a edição deste ano incluirá a hemofilia como tema central, contando com a presença dos principais stakeholders e palestrantes da área. Num momento de forte avalanche competitiva no mercado da hemofilia, a presença da Roche é estratégica, para podermos afirmar a nossa liderança no segmento das coagulopatias, garantindo a manutenção do share of voice, a presença junto dos decisores e a disseminação contínua das mensagens-chave do Hemlibra.

* Patrocínio do Congresso da APIH: 1800€
* Contrapartida: Presença de roll-up Hemlibra

Event Overview
To maximize the strategic impact of the Columvi launch in 2L DLBCL, we are focusing our resources on a national congress - Perspetivas em Hematologia 2027, a premier bi-annual national congress organized by ULS São João. Given the scarcity of high-level national medical events in Portugal, this congress is one of the most highly anticipated and attended gatherings for the national hematology community. For this edition, we would like to have a commercial booth and 1 of the only 3 available satellite symposium slots.

Strategic Context & Rationale
The DLBCL landscape in Portugal has rapidly evolved into an intensively competitive market, characterized by new indications approval for established therapies and the entry of several new market players. In order to effectively showcase the clinical value of Roche’s portfolio across the DLBCL area (Columvi in 2L DLBCL but also Polivy in 1L setting), it is critical to step up our Share of Voice (SOV) through highly visible, impactful scientific platforms/tools.

Expected Impact
The first Quarter of 2027 represent a critical window to establish momentum and shape therapeutic choices. Securing a prominent presence at this landmark congress will allow us to drive peer-to-peer scientific engagement, strengthen relationships with key national stakeholders, and set a strong baseline for the long-term performance of our hematology franchise.
Investment: 26,5K

* Sponsor Silver: 14K€ symposia + 7,5K stand, 10 registration of invitees

* 2 National speakers (experienced) and 1 moderator: up to 5K

items.itemName: PT_OPHTHA - S1.26 - Shaping the future of the retina ecosystem by partnering with GER TAEs
subitems: Pedido para apoio da publicação da metodologia usada na construção das guidelines
items.description:
GER (Grupo de Estudo da Retina) associates are a group of TAEs and key influencers, who shape the retina ecosystem in Portugal: this scientific association is responsible for the national guidelines’ update and manages the only patient registry that exists for retinal diseases in Portugal. In 2025, we have sponsored their associates’ Spring meeting, a working meeting, where they usually discuss their plan of action for the following months. This was a very successful event for Roche, as it allowed us to establish ourselves as a differentiated partner (through the format and style of the meeting, together with the topics aligned for the discussion, which were highly appreciated) and also for the retina landscape since a Consensus Document highlighting Good Practices for IVTs was produced.
For next year we would like to partner with them again by sponsoring GER’s Spring meeting in 2026, focusing on achieving three shared strategic objectives for the Portuguese retina ecosystem and promoting roundtables to discuss:
* The latest updates in nAMD treatment. Since we know that GER aims to update its nAMD guidelines in 2026, promoting this discussion is a true triple win in this moment in time;
* The impact of VABYSMO in capacity issues and burden reduction to the healthcare system and patients, supported by the dissemination of data from other countries with longer and proven experience with VABYSMO and its added-value;
* The need of an improved and systematic collection of RW data on retinal diseases management in SNS, so that the RWE generation for VABYSMO is assured to promote confidence.
We therefore propose to sponsor GER's Spring meeting and organize a 3-hour session with an external vendor with agile coaches to promote the discussions and collect the feedback and consensus.

Initiative Performance indicators:
S/M term - Event feedback (EpiCx); event indicators ( no. participants, etc); VoC
M/L term - Brand perception assessment; Partner Score

Despite being organized locally, ETAT has a national impact with attendees and faculty from all the country and a strong presence of P1 accounts. This year’s meeting takes place on April 18th at Quinta das Lágrimas - Coimbra.

As a reminder, Roche portfolio of targeted therapies includes alectinib and entrectinib (“mature”) and we are currently conducting phase III trials for our KRAS molecule - divarasib (Portugal is a recruiting country for both KRAScendo 1 [recruitment closed], 2 and 3 [expected to start enrollment in 2026]).

ESMO 2025 marked a special moment in Alectinib’s story as the ALEX trial came to a close, reporting the first OS data for an ALK TKi! An impressive 81 months mOS, for a subtype of aggressive NSCLC, whose course was completely changed by the introduction of alectinib.

As we face aggressive competition from a next generation ALK TKi (Lorlatinib), we need to protect Alectinib’s position, by highlighting the breadth of data of our molecule in advanced disease (only TKi with OS report, 3 consistent phase 3 trials, Real World experience of 7 years in clinical pratice), but also as the only ALK TKi approved for early stage disease (curative setting) during a 1h symposium in 2026 ETAT.

items.description:
“ Lung Cancer Fight Club” is the third edition of the Fundação Champalimaud’s Lung Cancer meeting, and for this meeting, the focus will be on the entire spectrum of lung cancer management, from early-stage to advanced cancer. The session "Fighting for cure in early stage NSCLC” is a perfect match for Roche's most recent advancements in the curative setting with alectinib and atezolizumab.
The broader Roche portfolio, which includes atezolizumab (for various stages of NSCLC and SCLC) and targeted therapies like alectinib and entrectinib, aligns with the ongoing debate about the future of drug development and treatment, and in addition to that, we are currently conducting phase III trials for our KRAS molecule - divarasib (Portugal is a recruiting country for both KRAScendo 1 [recruitment closed], 2, and 3 [expected to start enrollment in 2026].

Recently, the ESMO 2025 marked a special moment in Alectinib’s story as the ALEX trial came to a close, reporting the first OS data for an ALK TKi! An impressive 81 months mOS, for a subtype of aggressive NSCLC, whose course was completely changed by the introduction of alectinib.
Our PI from this trial, Tony Mok, presented those data at ESMO, and will be one of the speakers in the “Lung Cancer Fight Club Meeting”.

Additionally, the meeting is composed of a series of round tables that involve diverse stakeholders (health ministry, private insurers, patients) and has a high potential to bring together and leverage stakeholders from different national accounts.

Our presence reinforces our commitment to early-stage lung cancer and allows exposure of our brand/indication (Tecentriq and Alecensa) in a highly competitive and volatile treatment landscape.

Em Outubro de 2026 realiza-se o congresso do Grupo de estudos do Cancro do Pulmão (periodicidade 2-2 anos), o maior evento nacional dedicado à area terapêutica. Este ano é nossa ambição estarmos presentes com um simpósio médico dedicado à temática do CPNPC KRAS G12C. Esta mutação é a mais frequente no CPNPC e o desenvolvimento de novas terapêuticas para o seu tratamento é uma Hot Topics do momento. A nossa molécula dirigida ao KRAS - divarasib (potencial Best in Class), tem primeiros read outs (potencial 1ª indicação) esperados em meados de 2026. Portugal foi país recrutador nesse estudo, tendo a decorrer dois estudos pivotais adicionais com a molécula.
A presença com um simpósio permite-nos marcar o nosso investimento neste espaço competitivo e de elevado interesse, preparando a nossa presença futura.

items.description:
In 2024, the ULS Gaia-Espinho (ULSGE) ophthalmology service took significant steps toward modernization through the Integrar + Program. Building on this momentum, a new partnership is proposed to implement a Value-Based Healthcare (VBHC) Retina Clinic. This initiative aims to transition from volume-based care to a value-centered model, optimizing patient outcomes and healthcare sustainability.
Key Objectives
Optimize Patient Journeys: Streamline pathways for retinal pathology, reducing unnecessary visits through non-presential evaluations.
Enhance Outcomes: Improve patient satisfaction and quality of life via specialized follow-up and multidisciplinary care.
Establish a Scalable Model: Use this pilot as a "tailor-made" methodology that can be replicated across other hospital settings.
Project Scope & Implementation
The partnership will focus on three core pillars:
Pathway Co-creation: Defining clinical journeys, inclusion criteria, and relevant metrics, including CROMs (Clinical Reported Outcome Measures) and PROMs (Patient Reported Outcome Measures).
Digital Integration: Implementing a live dashboard for ophthalmologists to monitor real-time patient data at both individual and group levels.
Training: Providing comprehensive support and training for the ULSGE Retina team.
Partnership & Impact
As a strategic partner, Roche will support the implementation and pathway definition. The project will generate two comprehensive reports—at baseline and after one year—analyzing treatment adherence, clinical outcomes, and societal impact (PREMs). This data-driven approach is expected to highlight the clinical value of innovative treatments like Vabysmo within a real-world, value-based framework.

Advances in molecular oncology have transformed the treatment landscape of HR+, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer, with the identification of PIK3CA, AKT, and PTEN mutations as key drivers of endocrine resistance and therapeutic response. However, despite growing evidence, important knowledge gaps remain regarding the epidemiology, testing methodologies, patient selection and optimal clinical integration of targeted therapies directed at this pathway.
The Challenging Topics booklet will serve as an authoritative and accessible reference, aiming to:
- Highlight the relevance of PIK3CA pathway alterations in breast cancer — including their epidemiology, prognostic implications, and therapeutic potential.
- Review approved and emerging methods for molecular detection of PIK3CA/AKT/PTEN mutations, emphasizing their clinical applicability.
- Explore the role of PI3K pathway inhibition in combination with CDK4/6 inhibitors and endocrine therapy for luminal/HER2– metastatic breast cancer.
- Summarize the pharmacologic and clinical development of PI3K pathway inhibitors, including data on efficacy and safety from pivotal trials.

The booklet will be developed in collaboration with national experts, ensuring both scientific rigor and practical relevance.

A total of 500 printed copies will be produced for distribution to oncology centers, hospitals, and specialists, supporting ongoing medical education and evidence-based clinical decision-making.
The estimated budget for the project covering scientific coordination, content development, editorial production, design, and printing (22.755€).
Definition of Done: Booklet finalized, printed, and distributed to stakeholders.

items.itemName: PT_MS_S1.26 – Icobrain MS: Improving Patient Monitoring
items.description:
Context and Rationale: Neuroradiology plays a crucial role in the diagnosis, monitoring, and long-term management of patients with multiple sclerosis (MS). 
Need: Accurately interpreting MRI scans remains a significant challenge in monitoring MS disease activity. Early identification of patients with subclinical disease activity or radiological progression is essential to optimize therapeutic decisions and prevent disability accumulation.

Solution: To address this need, Roche Portugal proposes a partnership with SPNR and Icometrix to implement the Icobrain MS software (https://www.icometrix.com/multiple-sclerosis ) in four key hospitals across Portugal. Icobrain MS is an automated MRI analysis software that quantifies brain atrophy and lesion load, compares longitudinal scans, and generates standardized reports to support neuroradiologists and neurologists in detecting subtle disease activity and progression. 

Key WP Elements
Collaboration between Roche Portugal, SPNR, and Icometrix to implement Icobrain MS in 4 strategic hospitals with neuroradiologists dedicated to MS, capacity and interest in advanced imaging tools

Scope and Duration: Two-year phased implementation (2026–2027), ensuring training, technical integration, and data standardization.

Training course on MS for primary healthcare providers: [Scientific support: Multiple Sclerosis Study Group (GEEM) and the Portuguese Association of General Practice and Family Medicine (APMGF)] – Promotion for this course will be handled by the APMGF and will take place nationwide in a hybrid format.

items.itemName: PT_MS_Book: Stories of Resilience and Success & Brain Health
items.description:
Purpose
In collaboration with SPEM (Portuguese Multiple Sclerosis Society) and Dr. Filipa Ladeira (Neurologist at CRI-MS), an opportunity has arisen to develop an initiative to empower MS patients to become true managers of their condition. The goal is to develop a book with four main components, allowing patients to contribute actively to health promotion and the prevention of disease progression:
1. Brain Health (incorporating Roche Global resources)
2. Impact of environmental, social, and well-being contexts on disease management (smoking, physical activity, sleep, weight, alcohol consumption, etc.)
3. Success stories and real-life patient testimonials

This book will serve as a reference guide for both patients and caregivers, helping them navigate the disease journey and promoting the normalization of daily life for those living with Multiple Sclerosis. This initiative reinforces Roche's differentiating role within the national ecosystem, consolidating our position as strategic partners in disease management. Consequently, we are able to sustain the legacy of Ocrevus while preparing the short-term positioning for Fenebrutinib.

Presentation and distribution of copies at MS events and patient meetings: GEEM 2026, World MS Day, and Patient Meetings (specifically: CRI, Coimbra, Matosinhos).

Com o objetivo de dar resposta a esta necessidade concreta e apoiar o bem-estar das enfermeiras, consideramos importante realizar mais uma edição do NursesConnect mas deste vez um pouco diferente, totalmente dedicada à prevenção de lesões associadas à prática clínica.

items.itemName: 7th Lung Cancer Course – Continues medical education
items.description:
The 7th edition, the Lung Cancer Course of the Portuguese Society of Pulmonology (SPP) has established itself as an essential benchmark in medical education and within the Thoracic Oncology landscape in Portugal. This year, the SPP has taken a strategic step in the event's evolution: for the first time, the course will be integrated with the joint meetings of the Committees for Oncological Pulmonology, Endoscopic Techniques, and Thoracic Surgery. This 3day format enhances scientific exchange, multidisciplinary discussion, and the integration of new generations into the dynamics of the Portuguese Society of Pulmonology.
The scientific program will be dynamic, up-to-date, and highly practical, bringing together senior specialists, young doctors, and clinical decision-makers directly involved in lung cancer management. This environment promotes scientific updates, the standardization of practices, and the creation of synergies between centers — with a direct impact on the quality of patient care.
As a company holding the most diverse portfolio in this therapeutic area, our presence solidifies our continuous investment in high-quality medical education. We recognize that we are currently seeing a renewal of Healthcare Professionals (HCPs) dedicated to lung cancer; therefore, we aim to proactively contribute to the training of physicians who are now beginning their journey in this specialty. Furthermore, this new model represents a strategic opportunity, as it consolidates three activities into a single event, anticipating a significant increase in the number of participants and, consequently, greater exposure to highly specialized and influential professionals in national clinical practice.
 €6K  (1logistics, anticipating the need for 3 nights' accommodation for 5 guests)
Logo on all materials sent to participants; 1 staff registration, with access to all sessions; 5 participant registration; Insertion of an institutional video during plenary sessions.

To accelerate Polivy’s adoption in 1L and to prepare the medical community for Columvi in 2L, we propose a Preceptorship for 10 key Portuguese Hematologists. By visiting high-volume reference center in Germany, participants will gain first-hand exposure to established clinical workflows in markets where these therapies are already fully funded and integrated into standard care.

Portugal is currently in the early stages of Polivy 1L uptake. Seeing "Real-World Evidence" in action at experienced sites will reduce clinical inertia.
Leveraging the "halo effect"—clinicians are most influenced by international peers who have already successfully managed the transition from R-CHOP to Pola-R-CHP.

Also, as Columvi enters the 2L setting, seeing the management of bispecifics (step-up dosing, CRS monitoring) in seasoned European centers will build the necessary confidence for local implementation.

Why Germany ?
•	This country has had Polivy funding in 1L since 2024, meaning they have a significant cohort of patients who have completed treatment. This allows for discussions on long-term outcomes, not just initial responses. 
•	Participants will observe the logistical "know-how"—from pharmacy reconstitution to nursing protocols for bispecifics—providing a blueprint for their own hospitals in Portugal.

Upon return, these clinicians will act as Local Influencers, sharing their international experience in the regional with peers. This creates a powerful "top-down" knowledge to update internal hospital protocols and accelerate access.

SPH is the only big national congress exclusively dedicated to Hematology in Portugal, this event is the premier platform for engaging with the medical community. It represents our most critical opportunity to consolidate Roche’s leadership. 

Our participation aims to reinforce the established value of Polivy in 1L while paving the way for Columvi in 2L. Given the evolving reimbursement landscape for Columvi, we are designing a flexible and high-impact presence that can adapt its messaging to the funding status at the moment.

We intend to move beyond a traditional booth by creating a differentiating and dynamic space. While the final tactical details are being refined to align with the Columvi latest market access updates, the focus remains on:
•	Solidifying Polivy as the Standard of Care in 1L.
•	Preparing the 2L landscape with a focus on medical readiness and the value of Columvi.
•	Promoting peer-to-peer exchange through innovative booth dynamics.
Key Outcome: To ensure Roche stands out as the partner of choice in Hematology, demonstrating our agility and commitment to bringing innovation to Portuguese patients.

items.itemName: PT_MS_S2.26 - Mapping the Patient Care Pathway: Time-Motion and Cost Analysis of SC vs. IV Therapies
items.description:
MTO: Lead and Drive OCR 
STO: Fuel Rapid and Broad uptake with OCR SC
Co-creation with MA and RWE teams

Recognizing that the adoption of Ocrelizumab SC (OCR SC) is still limited in certain hospitals (eg, ULS Santa Maria, ULS Loures-Odivelas) due to a perceived lack of economic benefit and operational superiority over the intravenous (IV) formulation, this study was specifically designed to provide the necessary evidence to overcome this barrier and accelerate the therapeutic switch, as well as to obtain evidence to position OCR SC in a better position compared to Ofatumumab (main competitor). 

By conducting a multi-center study (MOAI Simplified Approach) across strategic hospitals representing the Portuguese reality - including both centers with established SC experience and those yet to adopt the formulation - the project will quantify the impact on healthcare resource utilization (HCRU) and we expect that the data will influence all territory.

Through a time-motion analysis and direct cost estimation (staff, consumables, and facility overheads), the study will map the patient care pathway at ULS São João, ULS Algarve, and ULS Cova da Beira to provide high-visibility evidence of "slot" optimization and increased hospital capacity. items.itemName: PT_SMA_S2.26 - SMA360º, um olhar sobre a evolução dos fenotipos da doença
items.description:
Beyond neurologists and child neurologists, multidisciplinary teams who see SMA patients are composed by several other specialities such as physiatrists, orthopedics, pulmonologists, nutricionists, speech therapists, etc. One of the key pillars for 2026 is the acknowledgment by HCPs of the improvements beyond motor function in patients treated with risdiplam (like fatigue, bulbar function, posture, breathing/ventilation support, etc). Therefore, we want to gather all of these specialities in "one place" and give them voice about their perspective on the evolution of phenotypes in SMA. We are planning to organize 2 meetings (online) about the evolution of SMA phenotypes, with the presentation of these other specialities point of view, and taking this oportunity to remind/celebrate about 5 years of risdiplam EC approval, with updates on the long-term results (RAINBOWFISH, FIREFISH, SUNFISH and JEWELFISH trials), and RWE context, finalizing with clinical cases sharing.

Meeting 2: pulmonologist + nutricionist + speech therapist, sharing of SUNFISH + JEWELFISH trials, 2 adult clinical cases (w/risdiplam)

items.description:
In 2022, Roche’s ophthalmology team had the first opportunity to co-create a patient journey project with ULS Arrabida. With this partnership, it was possible to map and review this CRI patient journey. Additionally we supported the development and implementation of a Patient’s satisfaction survey, which was key for them to review its internal procedures and define improvement strategies. 
Now ULS Arrabida’s Ophthalmology CRI seeks to reassess patients' satisfaction to evaluate the evolution over the past two years. This initiative aims to measure the impact of the 2024 action plan and provide an updated evidence-based perspective to support strategic decision-making and budget allocation for the 2026-2027 cycle.

Patient: Ensures their feedback leads to tangible changes; monitors if previous improvements effectively enhanced the quality of care in retinal diseases.
Healthcare System: Strengthens the VBHC culture by transitioning from a one-off pilot to a continuous improvement cycle; promotes efficient resource reallocation based on longitudinal patient outcomes.
Roche: Consolidates Roche’s position as a long-term strategic partner in ophthalmology and provides real-world evidence on the evolution of the ecosystem.

items.itemName: PT_Lung_AH_WP26/12_6.º Curso de Atualização em Oncologia Torácica para Cirurgiões Torácicos
items.description:
This event was launched in 2021 as a result of a co-creation between Roche and SPCCTV (Portuguese Society of Cardiothoracic and Vascular Surgery). Over the past few years, the course has opened up to participation from other companies and is now a core component of SPCCTV’s main activities.

Supporting the event this year is of particular importance, given the imminent reimbursement of ALINA (Alecensa in the adjuvant setting).

Thoracic Oncology is a fundamental area of intervention in the daily clinical practice of thoracic surgeons. The emergence of new drugs and therapeutic indications has led to increased patient survival in both advanced and early stages. The course is primarily aimed at thoracic surgeons, although registration is also open to clinicians from other specialties.

A 1.ª edição da CURIA ONCOEXPERTS, organizada pela Sociedade Portuguesa de Oncologia, decorrerá entre os dias 17 e 19 de junho de 2026, no Curia Palace Hotel, constituindo uma iniciativa inovadora de formação avançada dirigida a especialistas em Oncologia.

Este evento diferencia-se do formato tradicional de reunião científica, privilegiando aprendizagem interativa, discussão multidisciplinar, pensamento crítico e aplicação prática, através de metodologias inovadoras e multidisciplinares.

Os conteúdos científicos respondem a necessidades concretas identificadas pelos oncologistas e centram-se em áreas emergentes e desafios atuais da prática oncológica, incluindo terapêuticas inovadoras, medicina de precisão, genómica, gestão de toxicidades, tomada de decisão em cenários complexos e sustentabilidade dos sistemas de saúde.

O apoio a esta iniciativa permite reforçar o compromisso da companhia com a educação médica contínua, inovação científica e melhoria da qualidade dos cuidados oncológicos, promovendo simultaneamente proximidade institucional junto da comunidade oncológica nacional.

We are not just optimizing health systems generally; we are clearing the bottlenecks in our specific disease areas.

It shifts the program from a broad educational initiative to a highly focused "Action Learning" incubator, giving us the bandwidth to engage deeply with each team (comprising hospital administrators, Clinical Directors and HCPs). 2026 representa o último ano de consolidação de Phesgo antes da entrada do biossimilar de pertuzumab no mercado. Prevemos um impacto direto no negócio de pertuzumab e uma ameaça nas taxas de conversão de Phesgo. As conquistas de 2026 irão contribuir para alcançar o target de 80% de conversão e para a sustentabilidade do nosso negócio em 2027. 

Com o objetivo de maximizar o uso de Phesgo identificámos 4 hospitais com potencial de expandir o uptake, que não têm barreiras comerciais e que são high adopters ao nível dos produtos SC Roche. Contudo, ainda não alcançaram a conversão target de 80%.  

De acordo com o que apurámos internamente a barreira para maximizar a conversão reside nas equipas de enfermagem: devido ao elevado volume de mútiplos produtos SC atualmente administrados, estas equipas enfrentam uma carga física significativa e o risco de lesões por esforço repetitivo. Como mecanismo de autoproteção, acabam por limitar a expansão de Phesgo. 

Propomos a realização de reuniões personalizadas por conta, estruturadas em 2 fases:
- Diagnóstico (Pre-work): Questionário/entrevista (criado com Terap. Ocupacional e Enf. Champion) para mapear os pain points no fluxo, organização, postura e equipamentos na administração SC.

Ocup. irá adequar a sua intervenção aos resultados cada hospital, transmitindo boas práticas de admin SC, ergonomia e estratégias de mitigação de lesões; Enf. Champion: irá partilhar insights práticos da realidade de um serviço com elevada adoção SC, demonstrando como as boas práticas eliminam as queixas físicas ao mesmo tempo que otimizam o fluxo de trabalho diário.

items.itemName: PT_HEMOPHILIA S3.26 - CoB EG Program: Congenital Bleeding-Disorders Evidence Generation Program at ULS Sta Maria (2Y project)
items.description:
THE PROBLEM
Critical clinical information - such as patient phenotypes, bleeding episodes, hospitalizations, specialized lab results, and treatments - is scattered across different administration registries, electronic health records, laboratory information systems and pharmacy platforms. This fragmentation makes it incredibly difficult to build a holistic clear view of care pathways. Clinicians routinely face long waiting times for IT departments for data extraction tickets, stalling the generation of timely clinical insights. 
Without a standardized common data model, it is a labor-intensive process for clinical boards and management to benchmark care outcomes, track real-time patient experiences, and efficiently generate data for medical publications or patient outcomes' documentation.

THE VISION
We want to co-create, with Congenital Bleeding-Disorders and Pharmacy Services of ULS Sta Maria, a collaborative real-world data platform, designed to unlock advanced clinical insights for Congenital Blood Disorders (such as Hemophilia A and Von Willebrand Diseases).  
Using Promptly's advanced Federated Data Platform, the program ingests, integrates, and harmonizes complex local hospital data (as patient phenotypes, bleed encounters, hospitalizations, treatments, and laboratory/imaging results) into a standardized common data model.  As Promply is already creating a data lake for ULS Sta Maria and harmonizing this data lake to OMOP's language (a shared language for healthcare data), health data will be analyzed securely on-premises and never leaves the hospital environment, guaranteeing absolute patient privacy.  
With this solution, clinicians can access an interactive dashboard and use an AI tool to ask complex medical questions and have real-time data metrics in seconds. This tool will enable clinicians and pharmacists to track patient outcomes over time, run automated management metrics, and build customized reports for department meetings and medical congresses.

APTH-ISTH workshop and peer-to-peer dinner
Ahead of upcoming market shifts (Altuvoct reimbursed Jun '26; MIM8/FREHEMGO EMA approval est. Oct '26), Roche has secured an exclusive opportunity as the only hemophilia company invited to host a symposium at the APTH-ISTH Joint Workshop in Oporto (Jan 28–30, 2027). This 3-day meeting features a dedicated bleeding disorders day, providing a key touchpoint to engage immunohemotherapists and other relevant professions. Our goal is to leverage peer advocacy to address adult unmet needs, share real-world experience, and solidify Hemlibra as backbone of hemophilia treatment amidst new treatment options.
Key Deliverables & KOL Engagement
Roche Symposium: Keynote presentation by Prof. Cedric Hermans—a leading TAE and strong Hemlibra advocate who is also delivering the workshop's plenary STATE OF ART session— now and future.
Peer-to-Peer Advisory Dinner: An intimate dinner hosted by Prof. Hermans for 6–8 Portuguese HCPs titled "How to Select the Right Treatment Option Amidst Increasing New Alternatives." Through clinical case discussions, Prof. Hermans will draw on his early experience with emerging therapies (e.g., Altuvoct) to guide local physicians on how to choose the right treatment option for the right patient.
Why TRADE-OFF? 
Taking in consideration the life cycle and imminence of competitors in the severe Hemophilia space, the team thought of this activity to create a bigger impact than the international WFH congress. As symposia organizer at the APTH-ISTH workshop, Roche will be the only player present with symposia in the Hemophilia A space. 
Budget & Success Metrics
The estimated project cost of €13,000 will be offset by reducing 4 participants from the approved WFH Congress delegation (€12,000), yielding a budget-neutral activity.

NPS > 70% across both events among Immunohemotherapists.

This Work Package is designed to accelerate Evrysdi’s leadership by building deep HCP confidence in its compelling clinical value and patient benefits compared to competitor. The Mediconsult Wet Lab project work package focuses on the technical and clinical training of ophthalmic surgeons in the safe and precise implantation and refill procedures of the Contivue/Susvimo system. This package encompasses the coordination of physical training infrastructure, including the provision of artificial eyes and specialized surgical kits, and the delivery of a structured educational curriculum .

The Account Segmentation work package for Contivue involves the strategic classification and prioritization of Swiss ophthalmology centers based on their surgical infrastructure, patient volume for nAMD/DME, and readiness to adopt the Susvimo/Contivue technology and referral flow

The Content Clearing Process work package for Contivue defines the end-to-end framework for the medical, legal, and regulatory (MLR) approval of all promotional and educational assets, ensuring strict adherence to Swiss requirements and the Global blueprint.

subitems: Congresso Sociedade de Pediatria do DF
items.description:
The C1 actions proposed for this workpackage aim to establish an integrated and robust approach to the pediatric journey. Through omnichannel strategies, we seek to accelerate protocol adoption among professionals already treating nINH patients, while expanding Hemophilia A awareness among those not yet specialized. Complementing the digital front, the strategy will be refined through Advisory Boards and specialized consultancy, ensuring that specialty development is anchored in real-world market needs.
Speaker Training will empower influential voices to raise awareness, foster active patient searching, and identify opportunities for AI integration within blood centers. Simultaneously, high-level medical education initiatives, such as the Global Pediatric Preceptorship, will bridge local expertise with international best practices. Ultimately, this ecosystem aims to optimize hemophilia communication for pediatricians, equipping them to recognize clinical signs, achieve early diagnosis, and ensure seamless patient referral.

Context
Following the successful execution of the national HER2 Leadership Summit, which effectively shaped the medical debate around strategic treatment sequencing and the "Prisma Concept", there is a critical requirement to amplify this scientific positioning at a regional level. To proactively address evolving clinical beliefs and ensure consistent alignment across the oncological community, Roche Medical Affairs needs to decentralize these high-level discussions and adapt them to local realities.  
Objective
To establish and mobilize a coordinated network of local medical replicators (Summit faculty and key regional TAEs) to drive peer-to-peer scientific dissemination. This initiative will scale the Summit's legacy through localized activities, reinforcing phenotype-specific treatment frameworks and securing the clinical value of the Roche HER2 portfolio across major regional centers.

items.itemName: C2/C3 - 2026 [PRIVATE] HER2 Replicator Network: Local Dissemination
items.description:
Context
Following the successful execution of the national HER2 Leadership Summit, which effectively shaped the medical debate around strategic treatment sequencing and the "Prisma Concept", there is a critical requirement to amplify this scientific positioning at a regional level. To proactively address evolving clinical beliefs and ensure consistent alignment across the oncological community, Roche Medical Affairs needs to decentralize these high-level discussions and adapt them to local realities.  
Objective
To establish and mobilize a coordinated network of local medical replicators (Summit faculty and key regional TAEs) to drive peer-to-peer scientific dissemination. This initiative will scale the Summit's legacy through localized activities, reinforcing phenotype-specific treatment frameworks and securing the clinical value of the Roche HER2 portfolio across major regional centers.

This work package will assess participation (as appropriate w/ compliance considerations) and pull-through of existing skill programs, establish a clear view of skill maturity across functions aligned with the evolved Commercialization Capabilities Framework, and focus on enhancing the pull-through of existing and/or developing 1–2 new critical skill areas (e.g. omnichannel, segmentation) to enable commercialization excellence* in 2026. 

*Commercialization excellence incl. strategic, customer & competitive excellence 
**CC CoE Supported Program, ***Not a CC CoE Supported Program (brands have decided to rollout individually)

items.itemName: Root Cause Analysis and action plan to address contract near misses
subitems: Phase 1 - Conduct Lean Six Sigma workshop to determine root causes and gather baseline data for Contract Near Misses and then post RoME/MSA data for comparison.
Phase 2 - Development of an action plan aligned with existing work streams across functional teams  (eg new SLAs, timelines, training) to address identified root causes
Phase 3 - Execute the approved action plan and drive behavioural shift, driving new WoW etc and conduct post-implementation analysis showing sustained reduction in Contract Near Misses
items.description:
This Work Package (WP) is being launched to assess what is driving Contract Near Misses* in event execution. This issue has been identified in E&I as a Risk and Opportunity. Internal (and in some cases, external) inefficiencies create delays, increase pressure on support teams, and reduce consistency in execution. Interim Impact & Unknowns: Current work is already underway that may address or impact this problem, including: 
1. Master Service Agreements (MSAs): The launch of MSAs for Patients and HCPs (target February 1, 2026)  may have an impact on Contract Near Misses 
2. RoME Adoption: The launch and adoption of RoME is another unknown factor that may significantly impact the current execution process.

Understanding the root causes will enable clear end-to-end accountability through defined RACI roles, while uncovering opportunities to drive greater efficiency and consistency across the process.

Phased Approach Rationale: We will evaluate the work associated with solution implementation and execution once the root cause has been determined to see what existing work streams can action it, as well as the impact of the MSAs and RoME assessments.
*baseline data will also be used to determine which contract types are in scope based on frequency (eg are HCP contracts the sole type of contracts or is it more widespread including other stakeholder contracts?)

The current systemic imbalance, employee burnout, and declining engagement (as evidenced by low GEOS scores) stem from existing passive leadership behaviours that cannot sustain ambitious performance. Focusing on High Impact Leadership Effectiveness with an emphasis on collective leadership capability is the solution and will provide us with a competitive edge because it enables:
1. Strict Prioritization: Demands honest conversation and collective commitment to resource trade-offs, eliminating overload.
2. Joint Accountability: Drives active, cross-functional ownership of systemic balance to increase accountability in employee wellness
3. Sustainable Capacity: Ensures we meet "must-win country" goals through shared effort and delegation, not individual sacrifice.

Active and collective ownership in building a thriving leadership community that focuses their efforts on learning and growing their skills in courageous and visionary leadership is necessary to achieve our ambitions.

items.description: The WBO Tech Suite was rolled out in mid-2025. Although there was a significant amount of effort from the deployment team (global and local) adoption has been inconsistent. Some teams have reverted to previous, more user-friendly tools as they define them (e.g., Trello) thus the vision of the WBO Tech Suite is not being fully realized yet. The scope of this WP is to first understand the current adoption gaps and user pain points. We will then work to address them by demonstrating how the WBO Tech Suite provides similar or superior functionality, removing blockers, and creating a uniform plan for its use. Our approach will be supported by global, as these adoption challenges are not isolated to local. As a must-win country, we will identify areas requiring global support and collaboration and, in turn, share our work and learnings with other countries.
